item.text:
**3B.2 Research Note**

**Assessment:** mostly negative. In 2024, the best evidence points to ongoing abuse by Indonesian security forces in Papua and weak accountability from police/military institutions. There is one real positive signal: the army publicly apologized and detained 13 soldiers after a torture video surfaced. But that looks reactive, not a sustained pattern of prevention or punishment. I did not find credible evidence that Jokowi meaningfully addressed militias, party enforcers, or tolerated vigilantes as a distinct 2024 issue.

**Accepted Claims**
- **“2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Indonesia”** | **U.S. Department of State** | **published 2025-08-12; covers 2024** | [URL](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128570.html) | The report says there were credible reports of arbitrary killings, torture, arbitrary arrest/detention, and serious abuses in Papua; it also says the government did not systematically take credible steps to identify and punish officials who committed abuses, and that police/military often did not investigate or disclose findings. This is the strongest broad evidence of tolerance through weak accountability. | **3B.2**, **3B.1**, **2B.9**
- **“If It’s Not Racism, What Is It?”: Discrimination and Other Abuses Against Papuans in Indonesia** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-09-18** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/report/2024/09/18/if-its-not-racism-what-is-it/discrimination-and-other-abuses-against-papuans-in) | HRW says Indonesian security forces committed arbitrary arrests, detention, torture, extrajudicial killings, and mass forced displacement in Papua, and were seldom held to account. That supports a negative finding on prevention/punishment. | **3B.2**, **3B.1**, **2B.9**
- **Indonesian army apologizes after torture video goes viral** | **Reuters / Yahoo News** | **2024-03-25** | [URL](https://www.yahoo.com/news/indonesian-army-apologises-viral-papua-124111048.html) | The army apologized and said 13 soldiers were arrested after a video showed torture of a Papuan man in custody. This is the clearest positive evidence, but it is reactive and limited to a specific incident. | **3B.2**, **3B.1**, **2B.9**
- **Indonesian Army Apologizes After Torture Video Goes Viral** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-03-28** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/28/indonesian-army-apologizes-after-torture-video-goes-viral) | HRW reports the military apologized to Papuans and detained 13 soldiers, but stresses that abuses were serious and that accountability should extend beyond foot soldiers. This shows some punishment, but not robust prevention. | **3B.2**, **3B.1**, **2B.9**
- **Annual Overview 2024** | **Papuans Behind Bars** | **2025-07-23; covers 2024** | [URL](https://papuansbehindbars.org/annual-overview-2024/) | The overview records 370 political arrests in 2024, with most detainees released within hours or days and only a small number prosecuted. This shows continued coercive policing, while also indicating not all detentions became long prison terms. | **3B.2**, **3B.1**, **2B.9**

**Search Gap**
- I found **no strong 2024 evidence** that Jokowi dismantled, reined in, or systematically punished abusive police/military behavior beyond the March torture case response.
- I also found **no direct 2024 evidence** that party enforcers, informal loyalists, or vigilantes were a central, openly tolerated tool of regime control under Jokowi in the security sense asked here.
- The record is concentrated in **Papua**. Outside Papua, the evidence for this lens is much thinner.
